The Ducks were led by seventh year head coach [[Dana Altman]]. They played their home games at [[Matthew Knight Arena]] as members of the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac–12 Conference]]. They finished the season 33–6, 16–2 in Pac-12 play to win a share of the regular season Pac-12 championship. They defeated [[2016–17 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]] and [[2016–17 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]] in the [[2017 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]] before losing in the final to [[2016–17 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they defeated [[2016–17 Iona Gaels men's basketball team|Iona]], [[2016–17 Rhode Island Rams men's basketball team|Rhode Island]], [[2016–17 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]], and [[2016–17 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] to advance to the Final Four, marking the longest span between appearances in NCAA history (78 years), where they lost to the eventual champions [[2016–17 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]]. ==Previous season== {{main|2015–16 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team}} The [[2015–16 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Ducks]] finished the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] 31–7, 14–4 in [[2015–16 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 play]] to win the regular season conference championship. As the No. 1 seed in the [[2016 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac–12 Tournament]], the Ducks defeated [[2015–16 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]], [[2015–16 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]], and [[2015–16 Utah Utes men's basketball team|Utah]] to win the Pac-12 Tournament championship and earn the conference's automatic bid to the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As a No. 1 seed in the West Region, they defeated [[2015–16 Holy Cross Crusaders men's basketball team|Holy Cross]], [[2015–16 Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball team|Saint Joseph's]], and [[2015–16 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] to advance to the Elite Eight.
